_README: Deployment presets for liveClassifierTorchROS.py. This file is COMMITTED TO GIT so a
deployment site picks up new models and operating points with a plain `git pull` --
no environment variables to set on-site.
The FIRST entry of "configurations" is the one used at startup. To switch, either
reorder the list (and commit) or pass the preset name as an argument:
ros2 run magician_vision_classifier liveClassifierTorchROS --config low_false_alarm
The model's .pth/.json are auto-downloaded on first run from
http://ammar.gr/magician/models/CameraV2Models/ (ModelDownload.ensure_model), the same
directory scripts/uploadModels.sh pushes to.
gate.threshold semantics depend on gate.mode. Under the default "defect_mass" it
thresholds 1 - P(clean) -- the total probability mass on ANY defect class -- NOT the
max softmax probability. A max_prob threshold of the same number means something
completely different. Thresholds are NOT portable between models: re-read them from
that model's <name>_threshold_curve.json.
2026-09-09 -- NEW OPTIONAL FIELD: "cascade" (see the "default" entry below for the
full shape). Each configuration may carry a "cascade" block alongside its single-model
"model"/"gate": {enabled: bool, stages: [{model, step, gate: {mode, threshold, ...}},
...]}. When runtime.cascade_enabled() is true AND every listed stage's .pth/.json
resolves, liveClassifierTorch(ROS) builds an ORDERED CascadeClassifierPnm chain instead
of the single model or the two_stage ensemble -- stage 0 screens every tile at its own
step; each later stage re-tiles only what the previous stage promoted, at ITS OWN step,
and re-checks with its own threshold. This is a genuinely different mechanism from
runtime.two_stage (which majority-votes N models with no per-member threshold, reusing
stage 1's tiles verbatim) -- see knowledge/7-9-report.md SS8.4-SS8.7 for the methodology,
the validated squeezenet1_1->convnext_tiny result, and the caveats (linear compute-cost
Hz model, only measured on an A6000 dev box, not yet on real 5090 hardware). Cascade
stage step/threshold are NOT retunable per-frame like the single-model gate is -- a
cascade's value is a jointly-tuned set of per-stage operating points chosen offline;
retuning means switching presets. "cascade.enabled" is false in every preset below
until a real cascade-trained model pair is uploaded under deployment names -- read the
"default" entry's own cascade._note before flipping it on.
Every number under "measured" is read from the named threshold-curve file, not
estimated. They come from the run's held-out split, which was ALSO used to select the
checkpoint, so treat the absolute values as slightly optimistic -- the ranking between
operating points is sound (see ISSUES.md M3).
2026-09-09 UPDATE (MODEL SWITCH) -- READ BEFORE TRUSTING THE NUMBERS BELOW.
Model switched from ttcnxpico_convnext_pico back to ttcnxtiny_convnext_tiny -- the SAME

(dataloader.frozen_tile_split, sibling-leakage expected by design; NOT the older
coverage-carve-out fzcnxtiny_convnext_tiny from 2026-08-25), just the other

runtime.step DELIBERATELY KEPT AT 16, not changed to 18 -- an explicit operator call,
made knowing that convnext_tiny's own ISOLATED model-forward-pass bench at step 16 is
~13.5 Hz raw / ~21.6 Hz at the 5090-scaling this campaign uses, below the 23 Hz gate
(phase4_inference_bench.json; the 2026-08-25 entry preserved below found the same thing
for this exact architecture, and moved to step 18 -- ~17.1 Hz raw / ~27.3 Hz scaled --
for that reason). That bench number is model-compute only; it has never included
rendering. This session's SS8.7/SS8.8 fixes (generate_heatmap, process_predictions_erode,
draw_heatmap) removed what had been the dominant non-model cost on the single-model
path, so the REAL total per-frame Hz at step 16 today is unmeasured and could plausibly
clear the gate even though the isolated model bench alone does not -- but this has NOT
been verified end to end on real hardware. Re-bench the full pipeline (not just
classify_tiles) at step 16 before trusting this on a real deployment box; step 18
remains the safer, previously-verified choice if step 16 turns out short.
gate.threshold = 0.960 is a DELIBERATE, explicit operator choice for a high, strict,
false-alarm-suppressing operating point (not the model's own KPI-optimal gate, which
is 0.655) -- read off ttcnxtiny_ep1_convnext_tiny_threshold_curve.json: 91.85%
detected, 0.54% false-alarm. This is close to, but slightly more permissive than, the
model's own config-calibrated 'deployment' marker (threshold 0.965, 91.47%/0.50%) --
both live side by side below as 'default' and 'low_false_alarm'.

ttcnxpico_convnext_pico's switch carried an explicit, dated end-to-end test (download
+ load + forward pass, confirmed against a clean directory -- see the PUBLISHING NOTE
preserved below). No equivalent verification exists for ttcnxtiny_convnext_tiny: a zip
(ttcnxtiny_convnext_tiny_20260827_060518.zip) sits in the local model-store directory
scripts/uploadModels.sh pushes from, and that script hardcodes ALLOW_ALL=1 (publishes
everything there regardless of upload_allowlist.txt) -- so IF it has been run since
2026-08-27, this model is very likely already live at the server URL above. But that
has NOT been directly confirmed, unlike every model switch before it in this file's
history. Before trusting a `git pull` on a real deployment box to fetch a WORKING
model: either verify http://ammar.gr/magician/models/CameraV2Models/
ttcnxtiny_convnext_tiny_*.zip exists and downloads/loads cleanly, or keep a local copy
of the .pth/.json next to this file on any box you deploy to (ensure_file() only
reaches the network if the local copy is missing). ClassifierPnm.ensure_file() calls
sys.exit(1) on a failed fetch -- a missing model on an unreachable/stale server would
kill the process at startup, not degrade gracefully.
--- preserved from the 2026-08-26 update (ttcnxpico_convnext_pico), for history ---
Model switched from fzcnxtiny_convnext_tiny (Aug26_78K, recording-disjoint coverage
carve-out, see the 2026-08-25 note preserved below) to ttcnxpico_convnext_pico -- a
FRESH convnext_pico retrain from `EXPERIMENT-traintest-split-sweep.md`'s in-distribution
train/test campaign. This switch was made WITHOUT the standard generalization safeguard
the rest of this file's history relies on:
- There is NO TIER_A / recording-disjoint coverage number for this checkpoint.
`eval_coverage.py` was never run against it -- this campaign has no coverage
carve-out at all (dataloader.exclude_frames + validation_dataset were both removed
from its config in favour of a RANDOM TILE-LEVEL split, sibling-leakage expected by
design -- see EXPERIMENT-traintest-split-sweep.md §1/§3). We do not know whether
this checkpoint generalises better or worse than fzcnxtiny_convnext_tiny.
- The gate/threshold_reference curve below is ALSO calibrated on that same leaky
random split, not the Aug26_78K factory val -- score_checkpoints.py drives off
whatever build_val_only(cfg) returns for a config, and for this one that is the
frozen_tile_split, not validation_dataset. So even the raw detected/false_alarm
numbers immediately below are optimistic relative to a real held-out set, on top of
the usual same-checkpoint-selection optimism the paragraph above already flags.
- What IS different and real: this run's training set is LARGER than every other run
in the campaign -- it includes the ~3,054 frames every other config carves out for
coverage evaluation (§2.5 of knowledge/24-8-report.md). More data, unknown net effect.
This was an explicit, informed decision (not an oversight) to ship on that basis anyway.
If you are reading this cold: the honest move is to run eval_coverage.py against
ttcnxpico_convnext_pico on the real coverage carve-out before trusting this over the
previous default, then update this note.
runtime.step reverted to 16 -- convnext_pico's own native front-row throughput (36.0 Hz
at step 16, knowledge/24-8-report.md §4/§7) rather than convnext_tiny's coarser step 18,
since the deployed architecture changed back to convnext_pico.

_comment: Measured operating curve for the default model. Read verbatim from
detected = fraction of DEFECT tiles flagged. false_alarm = fraction of CLEAN tiles
flagged; multiply by the tiles-per-frame count to get crosses per frame.
⚠ Same caveat as every traintest-sweep-campaign model in this file: this curve is
measured on the SAME random, leaky, tile-level split the model trained against
(frozen_tile_split, sibling leakage expected by design) -- NOT the Aug26_78K factory
val. Treat every number here as optimistic relative to a real held-out set, not just
'slightly' as the file-level README's usual caveat says. See the 2026-09-09 UPDATE
A false-alarm rate below ~0.15% is NOT reachable: the sweep bottoms out at threshold
